source: KNOWLEDGE.md (RWS meanings) plus GhostLab SPEC (The Instrument)
notes: Codex single source of truth for upright, reversed, keywords, and love, career, general lenses.
Voices (Mystic, Clinical, Skeptical) render tone on top of this core. Do not ship three fact decks.
Reversed display is a 180 degree rotation of the same imageAsset.
The Instrument does not reverse. Include it in the shuffle bag only when the setting is on.
Do not put the trademark Rider-Waite on the home screen or App Store name.
Credit Pamela Colman Smith 1909 in Guide.

cards.name: The Fool
cards.uprightMeaning: New beginnings, innocence, leap of faith, spontaneity, free spirit, unlimited potential, trust in the unknown.
cards.reversedMeaning: Recklessness, naivety, hesitation, fear of the unknown, missed opportunity, foolish risk.
cards.core: Pure potential stepping into the unknown with open heart.
cards.uprightLove: A new beginning or leap of faith in the heart, with innocent, open potential.
cards.uprightCareer: A spontaneous new start that trusts unknown potential more than a fixed plan.
cards.uprightGeneral: New beginnings and a leap of faith, trusting the unknown with an open spirit.
cards.reversedLove: Hesitation or a reckless risk in love, missing an opening out of naivety or fear.
cards.reversedCareer: A missed work opening, or a foolish risk taken without looking.
cards.reversedGeneral: Fear of the unknown, hesitation, or a reckless step that wastes the opening.
cards.imageDescription: Young traveler in a colorful tunic stands at a cliff edge looking upward, a small white dog at the heels, a bindle on a staff over the shoulder, a white rose in hand, mountains and a bright sun behind.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: The Magician
cards.uprightMeaning: Manifestation, willpower, skill, focus, resourcefulness, as above so below, having all tools needed.
cards.reversedMeaning: Manipulation, unused talent, scattered energy, illusion, self-deception.
cards.core: Focused intention turns idea into form.
cards.uprightLove: Focused will and skill can turn a felt connection into something real.
cards.uprightCareer: You already have the tools. Focused skill can make the idea take form.
cards.uprightGeneral: Willpower, skill, and focus turn an idea into form. The tools are already on the table.
cards.reversedLove: Manipulation or self-deception in a bond, talent left unused.
cards.reversedCareer: Scattered energy or unused skill at work, an idea that stays an illusion.
cards.reversedGeneral: Unused talent, scattered focus, or a trick played on yourself.
cards.imageDescription: Figure in red and white robes stands behind a table holding a wand, cup, sword, and pentacle. One arm raised with a wand toward the sky, the other pointing to the earth, an infinity symbol above the head, flowers and greenery around.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: The High Priestess
cards.uprightMeaning: Intuition, mystery, inner knowing, subconscious, sacred knowledge, stillness, divine feminine.
cards.reversedMeaning: Blocked intuition, secrets, surface thinking, disconnection from inner voice.
cards.core: The answer already lives inside. Listen in silence.
cards.uprightLove: Stillness and inner knowing matter more than what is said out loud.
cards.uprightCareer: Trust the quiet read on a situation rather than the surface brief.
cards.uprightGeneral: The answer already lives inside. Listen in silence.
cards.reversedLove: A secret or a blocked inner voice keeps the bond on the surface.
cards.reversedCareer: Surface thinking or ignored instinct leads the work off true.
cards.reversedGeneral: Blocked intuition, secrets, or a disconnection from the inner voice.
cards.imageDescription: Seated woman between black and white pillars marked B and J, a lunar crown, a scroll labeled TORA in her lap, a veil of pomegranates behind her, a crescent moon at her feet.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: The Empress
cards.uprightMeaning: Abundance, fertility, nurturing, creativity, sensuality, nature, maternal energy.
cards.reversedMeaning: Creative block, smothering, dependence, neglect of self, overindulgence.
cards.core: Life-giving, generative, nurturing force.
cards.uprightLove: Nurturing, sensual, abundant care that grows a bond.
cards.uprightCareer: A generative, creative stretch of work that wants patient tending.
cards.uprightGeneral: Abundance, creativity, and nurturing force. Life wants to grow here.
cards.reversedLove: Smothering, dependence, or self-neglect dries the well.
cards.reversedCareer: Creative block or overindulgence stalls the work.
cards.reversedGeneral: Creative block, smothering care, dependence, or neglect of self.
cards.imageDescription: Crowned woman on a lush throne in a wheat field, a heart-shaped shield marked with Venus, a flowing gown, forest and stream behind her.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: The Emperor
cards.uprightMeaning: Authority, structure, stability, leadership, discipline, fatherhood, clear boundaries.
cards.reversedMeaning: Tyranny, rigidity, domination, lack of discipline, weak boundaries.
cards.core: Order and protective structure through will.
cards.uprightLove: Clear boundaries and steady structure protect the bond.
cards.uprightCareer: Leadership through discipline and a stable frame instead of noise.
cards.uprightGeneral: Authority, structure, and clear boundaries. Order held by will.
cards.reversedLove: Domination or weak boundaries warp the bond.
cards.reversedCareer: Tyranny, rigidity, or a collapse of discipline at work.
cards.reversedGeneral: Tyranny, rigidity, domination, or a lack of discipline and boundaries.
cards.imageDescription: Bearded man in armor on a stone throne carved with rams heads, an ankh scepter in one hand and a globe in the other, barren mountains behind.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: The Hierophant
cards.uprightMeaning: Tradition, spiritual teaching, institutions, mentorship, conformity to proven systems, shared belief.
cards.reversedMeaning: Rebellion against dogma, personal spirituality, unconventional path, questioning authority.
cards.core: Wisdom transmitted through established channels or the decision to step outside them.
cards.uprightLove: A bond shaped by shared belief, mentorship, or a proven way of being together.
cards.uprightCareer: Mentorship and proven systems. Learn the house rules before rewriting them.
cards.uprightGeneral: Tradition, teaching, and shared belief. Wisdom through established channels.
cards.reversedLove: Questioning the inherited script of the relationship, or leaving dogma for a personal path.
cards.reversedCareer: An unconventional path at work, or a challenge to institutional authority.
cards.reversedGeneral: Rebellion against dogma, a personal path, or questioning authority.
cards.imageDescription: Crowned religious teacher seated between two pillars, a triple-cross scepter, two kneeling acolytes, crossed keys at his feet.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: The Lovers
cards.uprightMeaning: Love, harmonious partnership, meaningful choice, alignment of values, union.
cards.reversedMeaning: Disharmony, misalignment of values, indecision, temptation, broken trust.
cards.core: A choice that reveals what you truly value.
cards.uprightLove: Harmonious partnership and a choice that shows what you truly value.
cards.uprightCareer: A meaningful choice about alignment of values, bigger than any one person.
cards.uprightGeneral: Love, union, and a choice that reveals what you value.
cards.reversedLove: Disharmony, temptation, or broken trust. Values are out of line.
cards.reversedCareer: Indecision or a values clash splits the path at work.
cards.reversedGeneral: Disharmony, misaligned values, indecision, temptation, or broken trust.
cards.imageDescription: Nude man and woman stand beneath a radiant angel, a tree with a serpent behind the woman, a flaming tree behind the man, a mountain and sun between them.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: The Chariot
cards.uprightMeaning: Victory, determination, willpower, focused control, forward momentum, triumph over opposition.
cards.reversedMeaning: Lack of direction, loss of control, aggression, scattered force.
cards.core: Directed will moves through resistance.
cards.uprightLove: Determined, focused will can carry a bond through opposition.
cards.uprightCareer: Forward momentum and focused control. Drive the work through resistance.
cards.uprightGeneral: Victory through determination and directed will.
cards.reversedLove: Scattered force or a loss of control pulls the bond off course.
cards.reversedCareer: No direction, aggression, or scattered effort at work.
cards.reversedGeneral: Lack of direction, loss of control, aggression, or scattered force.
cards.imageDescription: Armored figure stands in a stone chariot under a starry canopy, drawn by a black sphinx and a white sphinx, a city and river behind.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Strength
cards.uprightMeaning: Inner courage, patience, compassion, gentle mastery, soft power over force.
cards.reversedMeaning: Self-doubt, weakness, insecurity, uncontrolled force or suppressed power.
cards.core: Strength expressed through gentleness and self-mastery.
cards.uprightLove: Patience and compassion are the stronger hold on the bond.
cards.uprightCareer: Gentle mastery and inner courage get more done than force.
cards.uprightGeneral: Inner courage, patience, and soft power over brute force.
cards.reversedLove: Self-doubt or uncontrolled force strains the bond.
cards.reversedCareer: Insecurity, suppressed power, or a harsh hand at work.
cards.reversedGeneral: Self-doubt, weakness, insecurity, or force that is either wild or locked down.
cards.imageDescription: A woman in white gently closes a lion's jaws, an infinity symbol above her head, a flower crown and a garlanded dress, a mountain behind.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: The Hermit
cards.uprightMeaning: Solitude, introspection, inner guidance, wisdom-seeking, soul-searching, temporary withdrawal for clarity.
cards.reversedMeaning: Isolation, loneliness, excessive withdrawal, refusal of needed guidance.
cards.core: The light of one's own inner lantern.
cards.uprightLove: A temporary withdrawal to hear your own guidance about the bond.
cards.uprightCareer: Step back and seek counsel from your own lantern before the next move.
cards.uprightGeneral: Solitude and inner guidance. Withdraw briefly to see clearly.
cards.reversedLove: Isolation or a refusal of needed guidance leaves the bond cold.
cards.reversedCareer: Excessive withdrawal, or ignoring help that the work needs.
cards.reversedGeneral: Isolation, loneliness, too much withdrawal, or a refusal of needed guidance.
cards.imageDescription: A hooded figure in a gray robe stands on a snowy peak, a lantern with a six-pointed star in one hand, a staff in the other.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Wheel of Fortune
cards.uprightMeaning: Cycles, change, turning points, destiny, luck, the flow of fate.
cards.reversedMeaning: Resistance to change, stuck patterns, setbacks, feeling of bad luck.
cards.core: Everything turns. Ride the wheel rather than fight it.
cards.uprightLove: A turning point in the bond. Ride the cycle rather than fight it.
cards.uprightCareer: A change of luck or a cycle turning at work. Move with it.
cards.uprightGeneral: Cycles, change, and turning points. Ride the wheel rather than fight it.
cards.reversedLove: Stuck patterns or resistance to change in the bond.
cards.reversedCareer: Setbacks and a feeling of bad luck from fighting the turn.
cards.reversedGeneral: Resistance to change, stuck patterns, setbacks, or a sense of bad luck.
cards.imageDescription: A wheel in the sky marked TORA and alchemical symbols, a sphinx with a sword on top, a snake descending, Anubis rising, four winged figures in the corners.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Justice
cards.uprightMeaning: Fairness, truth, accountability, cause and effect, integrity, ethical clarity, legal matters.
cards.reversedMeaning: Injustice, dishonesty, avoidance of responsibility, bias.
cards.core: Truth and consequence made visible.
cards.uprightLove: Fairness, truth, and accountability in the bond. Cause and effect are visible.
cards.uprightCareer: Integrity and ethical clarity. Own the consequence of the work.
cards.uprightGeneral: Fairness, truth, and accountability. Truth and consequence made visible.
cards.reversedLove: Dishonesty, bias, or avoided responsibility harms the bond.
cards.reversedCareer: Injustice or bias clouds a work or legal matter.
cards.reversedGeneral: Injustice, dishonesty, avoided responsibility, or bias.
cards.imageDescription: A crowned woman sits between pillars, a sword upright in her right hand and scales in her left, a red robe and a purple veil behind her.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: The Hanged Man
cards.uprightMeaning: Surrender, new perspective, voluntary pause, sacrifice, seeing from a different angle.
cards.reversedMeaning: Stalling, martyrdom, resistance to necessary delay, stuck without insight.
cards.core: Stillness that reveals what motion concealed.
cards.uprightLove: A voluntary pause that lets you see the bond from a new angle.
cards.uprightCareer: Surrender the old approach. A pause will show what motion hid.
cards.uprightGeneral: Surrender and a new perspective. Stillness reveals what motion concealed.
cards.reversedLove: Stalling or martyrdom in the bond, stuck without insight.
cards.reversedCareer: Resistance to a needed delay, or busy stalling at work.
cards.reversedGeneral: Stalling, martyrdom, resistance to a needed delay, or being stuck without insight.
cards.imageDescription: A man hangs upside down from a living T-shaped tree by one foot, the other leg crossed, a halo around his calm face, hands behind his back.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Death
cards.uprightMeaning: Transformation, endings that clear space, transition, release, rebirth (almost never literal death).
cards.reversedMeaning: Resistance to change, stagnation, fear of endings, incomplete transition.
cards.core: Necessary ending that makes new life possible.
cards.uprightLove: An ending that clears space so the bond can be reborn in another form.
cards.uprightCareer: A work chapter closes so a new one can start. Release what is finished.
cards.uprightGeneral: Transformation and release. A necessary ending that makes new life possible. Almost never literal death.
cards.reversedLove: Fear of an ending, or a transition left half done, keeps the bond stagnant.
cards.reversedCareer: Resistance to a needed close at work, or a change left incomplete.
cards.reversedGeneral: Resistance to change, stagnation, fear of endings, or an incomplete transition.
cards.imageDescription: An armored skeleton rides a white horse, a black banner with a white rose, a fallen king, a bishop, a child and a maiden, a sun rising between two towers beside a river.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Temperance
cards.uprightMeaning: Balance, moderation, patience, alchemy, integration of opposites, healing.
cards.reversedMeaning: Imbalance, excess, impatience, internal conflict.
cards.core: Harmonizing forces into something greater.
cards.uprightLove: Patience and a blend of opposites can heal the bond.
cards.uprightCareer: Moderate, patient mixing of forces. Do not rush the alloy.
cards.uprightGeneral: Balance, moderation, and the alchemy of opposites. Healing by blend.
cards.reversedLove: Imbalance, excess, or impatience strains the bond.
cards.reversedCareer: Internal conflict or excess throws the work off true.
cards.reversedGeneral: Imbalance, excess, impatience, or internal conflict.
cards.imageDescription: An angel with red wings pours water between two cups, one foot on land and one in water, a triangle on the chest, a path toward distant mountains and a sun.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: The Devil
cards.uprightMeaning: Attachment, addiction, materialism, shadow material, feeling trapped (often by own chains).
cards.reversedMeaning: Liberation, breaking free, awareness of patterns, reclaiming power.
cards.core: The chains are usually looser than they appear.
cards.uprightLove: Attachment or a feeling of being trapped in the bond, often by your own chains.
cards.uprightCareer: A material or habit bind at work. The chain may be looser than it looks.
cards.uprightGeneral: Attachment, addiction, and a feeling of being trapped, often by your own chains.
cards.reversedLove: Breaking free of a pattern and reclaiming power in the bond.
cards.reversedCareer: Awareness of a bind at work, and a move to reclaim power.
cards.reversedGeneral: Liberation, breaking free, seeing the pattern, reclaiming power.
cards.imageDescription: A horned, bat-winged figure perches on a black pedestal, an inverted pentagram on the forehead, a torch in the left hand, two horned human figures chained at the neck with loose chains.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: The Tower
cards.uprightMeaning: Sudden upheaval, revelation, collapse of false structures, breakthrough, necessary destruction.
cards.reversedMeaning: Averted crisis, fear of change, slow collapse, delayed truth.
cards.core: What was built on false foundations must fall.
cards.uprightLove: A sudden revelation or collapse of a false story in the bond.
cards.uprightCareer: A false structure at work falls. The breakthrough is the rubble.
cards.uprightGeneral: Sudden upheaval and necessary destruction of what was built on a false foundation.
cards.reversedLove: Fear of change or a delayed truth. The collapse is slow or narrowly averted.
cards.reversedCareer: An averted crisis, or a slow collapse you are still postponing.
cards.reversedGeneral: Averted crisis, fear of change, slow collapse, or delayed truth.
cards.imageDescription: A stone tower is struck by lightning, its crown blown off, flames from the windows, two figures falling, gray clouds and falling yods.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: The Star
cards.uprightMeaning: Hope, healing, inspiration, renewal, faith after difficulty, quiet optimism.
cards.reversedMeaning: Discouragement, lost faith, disconnection from hope.
cards.core: Light returns after the storm. Gentle and steady.
cards.uprightLove: Quiet hope and healing after difficulty in the heart.
cards.uprightCareer: Inspiration and renewal after a hard stretch of work.
cards.uprightGeneral: Hope, healing, and quiet optimism. Light returns after the storm.
cards.reversedLove: Discouragement or lost faith in the bond.
cards.reversedCareer: A disconnection from hope about the work.
cards.reversedGeneral: Discouragement, lost faith, or a disconnection from hope.
cards.imageDescription: A nude woman kneels at a pool, pouring water from two jugs, one onto land and one into water, a large yellow star above with seven smaller stars, a bird on a tree.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: The Moon
cards.uprightMeaning: Illusion, intuition, dreams, the subconscious, uncertainty, hidden fears or depths.
cards.reversedMeaning: Clarity emerging, confusion lifting, facing the shadow, releasing fear.
cards.core: Feel first, understand later. What is hidden wants to be known.
cards.uprightLove: Uncertainty, dreams, and hidden fears in the bond. Feel first, understand later.
cards.uprightCareer: The work is in a fog. Intuition and hidden material matter more than the brief.
cards.uprightGeneral: Illusion, intuition, and hidden depths. What is hidden wants to be known.
cards.reversedLove: Confusion lifts. Facing the shadow can release fear in the bond.
cards.reversedCareer: Clarity emerging at work as the fog thins.
cards.reversedGeneral: Clarity emerging, confusion lifting, facing the shadow, releasing fear.
cards.imageDescription: A full moon with a face hangs above a path between two towers, a crayfish crawls from a pool, a dog and a wolf howl, drops fall from the moon.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: The Sun
cards.uprightMeaning: Joy, vitality, success, clarity, warmth, childlike aliveness, radiance.
cards.reversedMeaning: Temporary clouding, dimmed joy, self-doubt, blocked vitality.
cards.core: Pure life-giving light made visible.
cards.uprightLove: Warmth, joy, and clear, childlike aliveness in the bond.
cards.uprightCareer: Success, clarity, and vitality in the work. The light is on.
cards.uprightGeneral: Joy, vitality, success, and warmth. Pure life-giving light made visible.
cards.reversedLove: Temporary clouding or self-doubt dims the joy in the bond.
cards.reversedCareer: Blocked vitality or a dimmed success at work. The cloud is temporary.
cards.reversedGeneral: Temporary clouding, dimmed joy, self-doubt, or blocked vitality.
cards.imageDescription: A large sun with a face shines above a smiling child on a white horse, sunflowers behind a gray wall, a red banner in the child's hand.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Judgement
cards.uprightMeaning: Awakening, calling, reckoning, rebirth, second chances, clarity of purpose, rising to a higher level.
cards.reversedMeaning: Self-doubt, ignored calling, harsh self-judgment, reluctance to rise.
cards.core: A clear summons to step into the next version of yourself.
cards.uprightLove: A reckoning and a second chance. Rise to a clearer version of the bond.
cards.uprightCareer: A calling and a rebirth of purpose at work. Step up a level.
cards.uprightGeneral: Awakening, calling, and a second chance. A summons to the next version of yourself.
cards.reversedLove: Harsh self-judgment or a reluctance to rise keeps the bond stuck.
cards.reversedCareer: An ignored calling or self-doubt about the next step at work.
cards.reversedGeneral: Self-doubt, an ignored calling, harsh self-judgment, or a reluctance to rise.
cards.imageDescription: An angel with a trumpet and banner appears in the clouds, figures rise from coffins below, mountains and water in the distance.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: The World
cards.uprightMeaning: Completion, wholeness, fulfillment, integration, successful cycle ending, celebration.
cards.reversedMeaning: Incomplete cycles, delayed closure, unfinished business, near-miss.
cards.core: Everything in its proper place. A cycle completed.
cards.uprightLove: Fulfillment and a successful cycle ending in the bond. Celebrate the whole.
cards.uprightCareer: A project or role reaches integration and a clean close.
cards.uprightGeneral: Completion, wholeness, and celebration. A cycle in its proper place.
cards.reversedLove: Unfinished business or delayed closure in the bond.
cards.reversedCareer: An incomplete cycle or a near-miss at work. Close what is open.
cards.reversedGeneral: Incomplete cycles, delayed closure, unfinished business, or a near-miss.
cards.imageDescription: A dancing nude figure is wrapped in a violet scarf inside an oval wreath, a wand in each hand, an angel, eagle, lion, and bull in the four corners.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Ace of Wands
cards.uprightMeaning: Creative spark, new passion, inspiration, potential, entrepreneurial beginning.
cards.reversedMeaning: Blocked creativity, hesitation, lack of direction, delayed start.
cards.uprightLove: A new spark of passion or creative heat in the heart.
cards.uprightCareer: An entrepreneurial beginning. Inspiration wants a first move.
cards.uprightGeneral: A creative spark and new passion. Potential is in the hand.
cards.reversedLove: Hesitation or a blocked spark delays a new passion.
cards.reversedCareer: A delayed start or no direction on a new project.
cards.reversedGeneral: Blocked creativity, hesitation, lack of direction, or a delayed start.
cards.imageDescription: A hand from a cloud holds a living wand with new leaves, a castle on a distant hill, a river and landscape below.
cards.core: A live spark handed to you: raw creative fire looking for its first act. The invitation is to strike while it is still warm.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Two of Wands
cards.uprightMeaning: Planning, future vision, personal power, deciding on a direction, looking outward.
cards.reversedMeaning: Fear of change, indecision, playing small, unclear plan.
cards.uprightLove: Looking outward together, deciding a shared direction.
cards.uprightCareer: Plan the next move. Personal power is in choosing a direction.
cards.uprightGeneral: Planning, future vision, and a decision about where to aim.
cards.reversedLove: Fear of change or playing small keeps the bond without a plan.
cards.reversedCareer: Indecision or an unclear plan stalls the work.
cards.reversedGeneral: Fear of change, indecision, playing small, or an unclear plan.
cards.imageDescription: A figure stands on a battlement holding a globe, one wand fixed to the wall and one in hand, looking out over a sea and mountains.
cards.core: The world in your hands and a choice of maps. Planning between horizons, safe ground versus the wider world.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Three of Wands
cards.uprightMeaning: Expansion, foresight, early results, ships coming in, leadership looking ahead.
cards.reversedMeaning: Delays, obstacles, limited vision, frustration.
cards.uprightLove: Early results in the bond. Look ahead rather than back.
cards.uprightCareer: Expansion and ships coming in. Lead by looking farther out.
cards.uprightGeneral: Expansion, foresight, and early results. The ships are coming in.
cards.reversedLove: Frustration or limited vision about where the bond is headed.
cards.reversedCareer: Delays and obstacles shrink the work's horizon.
cards.reversedGeneral: Delays, obstacles, limited vision, or frustration.
cards.imageDescription: A figure in a robe stands on a cliff with three planted wands, watching ships on a yellow sea, mountains on the far shore.
cards.core: Ships sent out and the long watch from the cliff. Expansion is underway, and what you set in motion is coming back toward you.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Four of Wands
cards.uprightMeaning: Celebration, homecoming, harmony, milestone, stable foundation, community joy.
cards.reversedMeaning: Tension at home, delayed celebration, lack of support, transition.
cards.uprightLove: A homecoming or milestone worth celebrating together.
cards.uprightCareer: A stable foundation and a communal milestone at work.
cards.uprightGeneral: Celebration, harmony, and a stable foundation. A milestone is here.
cards.reversedLove: Tension at home or a celebration delayed. Support is thin.
cards.reversedCareer: A transition or missing support undercuts the milestone.
cards.reversedGeneral: Tension at home, delayed celebration, lack of support, or a restless transition.
cards.imageDescription: A flowered canopy on four wands, two figures raise bouquets before a castle, a garland of fruit and flowers overhead.
cards.core: A milestone worth garlands: stable ground celebrated with people who matter. Rest inside the structure you built.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Five of Wands
cards.uprightMeaning: Competition, conflict, struggle, clashing energies, rivalry.
cards.reversedMeaning: Resolution, finding common ground, avoiding unnecessary conflict, internal struggle.
cards.uprightLove: Clashing energies or rivalry in the bond. The struggle is noisy.
cards.uprightCareer: Competition and clashing wills at work. Rivalry is in the room.
cards.uprightGeneral: Competition, conflict, and clashing energies.
cards.reversedLove: Common ground is possible, or the fight was never needed.
cards.reversedCareer: Resolution of a work clash, or the struggle turns inward.
cards.reversedGeneral: Resolution, common ground, avoided conflict, or an internal struggle.
cards.imageDescription: Five youths in colorful tunics brandish wands against one another in a chaotic contest, no one clearly winning, a blue sky above.
cards.core: Sticks raised in a scrimmage. Friction, competition, and crossed agendas that can sharpen you if the rules stay fair.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Six of Wands
cards.uprightMeaning: Victory, public recognition, success, pride, momentum, deserved praise.
cards.reversedMeaning: Ego, lack of recognition, private success only, fall from grace.
cards.uprightLove: A public, proud success in the bond. Praise that is earned.
cards.uprightCareer: Victory and public recognition. Momentum after a win.
cards.uprightGeneral: Victory, recognition, and deserved praise. Momentum is with you.
cards.reversedLove: Ego, or a success that stays private, cools the bond.
cards.reversedCareer: A lack of recognition at work, or a fall from grace.
cards.reversedGeneral: Ego, missing recognition, private success only, or a fall from grace.
cards.imageDescription: A rider on a white horse wears a laurel wreath and holds a wand topped with another wreath, a cheering crowd with wands around him.
cards.core: The laurel and the ride through the crowd. A win that wants witnessing, recognition earned and arriving.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Seven of Wands
cards.uprightMeaning: Defending position, standing ground, perseverance, courage under pressure.
cards.reversedMeaning: Overwhelm, giving up, exhausted defense, lack of confidence.
cards.uprightLove: Stand your ground in the bond. Courage under pressure.
cards.uprightCareer: Defend the work you have already won. Persevere.
cards.uprightGeneral: Defending a position, standing ground, courage under pressure.
cards.reversedLove: Overwhelm or a collapse of confidence in the bond.
cards.reversedCareer: An exhausted defense, or giving up the ground at work.
cards.reversedGeneral: Overwhelm, giving up, exhausted defense, or a lack of confidence.
cards.imageDescription: A figure on a height holds one wand against six rising from below, an uneven stance, a look of strain and resolve.
cards.core: The high ground held against many. Defending a position you believe in, advantage kept through nerve.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Eight of Wands
cards.uprightMeaning: Swift movement, rapid progress, news arriving, things accelerating.
cards.reversedMeaning: Delays, frustration, miscommunication, scattered energy.
cards.uprightLove: News arriving and the bond accelerating. Things move fast.
cards.uprightCareer: Rapid progress. Messages and work are in flight.
cards.uprightGeneral: Swift movement, rapid progress, news arriving.
cards.reversedLove: Miscommunication or delay frustrates the bond.
cards.reversedCareer: Scattered energy or stalled messages at work.
cards.reversedGeneral: Delays, frustration, miscommunication, or scattered energy.
cards.imageDescription: Eight living wands fly diagonally through a clear sky above a river and a house on a green hill. No figures.
cards.core: Eight shafts in full flight: sudden speed, news, and movement after delay. Things land quickly now.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Nine of Wands
cards.uprightMeaning: Resilience, last stand, perseverance, almost there, guarded strength.
cards.reversedMeaning: Exhaustion, paranoia, hyper-vigilance, refusing needed rest.
cards.uprightLove: Guarded strength in the bond. You are almost through this stretch.
cards.uprightCareer: A last stand of perseverance at work. Hold, then rest.
cards.uprightGeneral: Resilience and guarded strength. Almost there.
cards.reversedLove: Exhaustion or hyper-vigilance wears the bond. Rest is needed.
cards.reversedCareer: Paranoia or a refusal to rest after a long defense at work.
cards.reversedGeneral: Exhaustion, paranoia, hyper-vigilance, or a refusal of needed rest.
cards.imageDescription: A bandaged figure leans on a wand, eight more wands stand as a fence behind, a look of wary endurance.
cards.core: Wounded but standing, the last fence watched. Resilience near the finish, the strength to hold on one more round.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Ten of Wands
cards.uprightMeaning: Burden, overcommitment, hard work, carrying too much, responsibility.
cards.reversedMeaning: Release, delegation, setting burdens down, relief.
cards.uprightLove: Carrying too much in the bond. The load is real.
cards.uprightCareer: Overcommitment and hard work. Too many bundles in one pair of arms.
cards.uprightGeneral: Burden, overcommitment, and responsibility. You are carrying too much.
cards.reversedLove: Set a burden down together. Relief through sharing the load.
cards.reversedCareer: Delegate. Release what the role no longer needs to hold.
cards.reversedGeneral: Release, delegation, setting burdens down, relief.
cards.imageDescription: A figure bent forward carries a heavy bundle of ten wands toward a distant town, the face hidden by the load.
cards.core: Every stave carried at once, the harvest bent under its own weight. Completion is close, but so is the case for putting some of it down.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Page of Wands
cards.uprightMeaning: Enthusiastic beginner, exploration, new ideas, free spirit, playful energy.
cards.reversedMeaning: Lack of direction, scattered focus, immaturity, idea fatigue.
cards.uprightLove: Playful, beginner energy in the heart. New ideas that have not yet grown into a vow.
cards.uprightCareer: An enthusiastic first scout of a new idea at work.
cards.uprightGeneral: An enthusiastic beginner. Exploration, new ideas, playful energy.
cards.reversedLove: Scattered focus or immaturity in the bond. The spark has no aim.
cards.reversedCareer: Idea fatigue or no direction on a new brief.
cards.reversedGeneral: Lack of direction, scattered focus, immaturity, or idea fatigue.
cards.imageDescription: A young figure in a yellow tunic patterned with salamanders holds a living wand and studies its leaves, a barren landscape and distant pyramids behind.
cards.core: A student of fire: curiosity with a torch in its hand. News of a venture, or the stance of beginning boldly and learning loud.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Knight of Wands
cards.uprightMeaning: Bold action, adventure, passion, charging forward, high energy.
cards.reversedMeaning: Recklessness, impulsiveness, burnout, frustration.
cards.uprightLove: Bold, passionate pursuit. High energy in the bond.
cards.uprightCareer: Charge the work with adventure and heat. Move.
cards.uprightGeneral: Bold action, adventure, passion, charging forward.
cards.reversedLove: Reckless or impulsive heat burns the bond. Frustration follows.
cards.reversedCareer: Burnout or reckless motion at work without a line.
cards.reversedGeneral: Recklessness, impulsiveness, burnout, or frustration.
cards.imageDescription: An armored knight on a rearing horse holds a wand, a plume and salamander cloak, a desert and pyramids behind.
cards.core: Fire at full gallop: charisma, appetite, and haste in one rider. Magnificent momentum that benefits from a destination.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Queen of Wands
cards.uprightMeaning: Confidence, warmth, magnetic presence, creative leadership, courage.
cards.reversedMeaning: Insecurity, jealousy, demanding energy, faded light.
cards.uprightLove: Warm, magnetic, courageous presence in the bond.
cards.uprightCareer: Creative leadership with confidence and warmth.
cards.uprightGeneral: Confidence, warmth, magnetic presence, and courage.
cards.reversedLove: Jealousy, insecurity, or a demanding energy dims the bond.
cards.reversedCareer: Faded light or insecurity undercuts leadership at work.
cards.reversedGeneral: Insecurity, jealousy, demanding energy, or faded light.
cards.imageDescription: A crowned woman sits on a throne holding a sunflower and a wand, a black cat at her feet, lions on the throne, sunflowers behind.
cards.core: Fire mastered inward: warm, magnetic confidence that holds a room without raising its voice. Courage worn as ease.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: King of Wands
cards.uprightMeaning: Visionary leadership, charisma, big-picture thinking, decisive action.
cards.reversedMeaning: Domineering, impulsiveness, ego-driven leadership, all heat no plan.
cards.uprightLove: Charismatic, decisive vision in the bond. Eyes on the big picture instead of the squabble.
cards.uprightCareer: Visionary leadership and decisive action. See the whole field, then move.
cards.uprightGeneral: Visionary leadership, charisma, big-picture thinking, decisive action.
cards.reversedLove: Domineering or ego-driven heat in the bond. All heat, no plan.
cards.reversedCareer: Impulsive, ego-led management. Heat without a plan.
cards.reversedGeneral: Domineering, impulsiveness, ego-driven leadership, or all heat and no plan.
cards.imageDescription: A crowned man in a salamander cloak sits on a throne holding a living wand, lions on the throne, a small lizard at his feet.
cards.core: Fire mastered outward: vision with command. A leader who turns sparks into enterprises and expects the tribe to follow.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Ace of Cups
cards.uprightMeaning: New emotional beginning, heart opening, love, compassion, intuitive flow, creative inspiration of the heart.
cards.reversedMeaning: Blocked emotions, repressed feelings, emptiness, closed heart.
cards.uprightLove: A heart opening. New love or a new flow of compassion.
cards.uprightCareer: Creative inspiration of the heart applied to the work as much as to romance.
cards.uprightGeneral: A new emotional beginning. The heart opens and the cup overflows.
cards.reversedLove: A closed or empty heart. Feeling is blocked or repressed.
cards.reversedCareer: Repressed feeling dries the well that the work was drawing from.
cards.reversedGeneral: Blocked emotions, repressed feelings, emptiness, or a closed heart.
cards.imageDescription: A hand from a cloud holds a cup overflowing into a lotus pond, a dove with a host above the cup, a lush landscape.
cards.core: An offered cup running over: a new opening of the heart, feeling, or creative flow. Receive it before you analyze it.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Two of Cups
cards.uprightMeaning: Partnership, mutual attraction, harmony, connection, union.
cards.reversedMeaning: Imbalance, broken connection, miscommunication, separation.
cards.uprightLove: Mutual attraction and a harmonious partnership.
cards.uprightCareer: A working partnership built on mutual regard.
cards.uprightGeneral: Partnership, harmony, connection, union.
cards.reversedLove: Imbalance, miscommunication, or a broken connection.
cards.reversedCareer: A work partnership out of balance, or a split.
cards.reversedGeneral: Imbalance, broken connection, miscommunication, or separation.
cards.imageDescription: A man and a woman face each other, each holding a cup, a caduceus and a lion-headed winged figure above their joined hands, a house on a hill behind.
cards.core: Two cups meeting at eye level: mutual attraction, partnership, an exchange where both sides pour. The bond forms in the balance.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Three of Cups
cards.uprightMeaning: Friendship, celebration, community, joyful gathering, support.
cards.reversedMeaning: Overindulgence, gossip, isolation, third-party interference.
cards.uprightLove: Friendship and a joyful gathering around the bond.
cards.uprightCareer: Community support and a celebration of shared work.
cards.uprightGeneral: Friendship, celebration, community, and support.
cards.reversedLove: Gossip, isolation, or a third party interferes with the bond.
cards.reversedCareer: Overindulgence or gossip undercuts the team.
cards.reversedGeneral: Overindulgence, gossip, isolation, or third-party interference.
cards.imageDescription: Three women raise cups in a harvest dance, fruit and a pumpkin at their feet, vines and a clear sky.
cards.core: Cups raised in a circle of friends: celebration, community, the joy that only shows up in company.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Four of Cups
cards.uprightMeaning: Apathy, contemplation, emotional withdrawal, missing what is offered.
cards.reversedMeaning: New awareness, choosing to engage, acceptance, emerging from stagnation.
cards.uprightLove: Emotional withdrawal. An offered cup in the bond may be going unseen.
cards.uprightCareer: Apathy about an offer at work. Contemplation that misses what is in reach.
cards.uprightGeneral: Apathy, withdrawal, and missing what is being offered.
cards.reversedLove: Choosing to engage again. New awareness in the bond.
cards.reversedCareer: Acceptance and a return from stagnation at work.
cards.reversedGeneral: New awareness, choosing to engage, acceptance, emerging from stagnation.
cards.imageDescription: A seated figure under a tree crosses the arms, three cups on the grass, a hand from a cloud offers a fourth cup that goes unnoticed.
cards.core: A fourth cup offered from a cloud and a folded-arm refusal. Apathy or boredom guarding the moment when a real gift passes by.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Five of Cups
cards.uprightMeaning: Grief, loss, focusing on what is gone, disappointment.
cards.reversedMeaning: Acceptance, moving on, seeing what remains, healing.
cards.uprightLove: Grief and disappointment. The eye is on what spilled while two cups still stand behind you.
cards.uprightCareer: A loss at work. Look also at what remains.
cards.uprightGeneral: Grief, loss, and a focus on what is gone.
cards.reversedLove: Healing. See what remains in the bond and move on.
cards.reversedCareer: Acceptance of a work loss. Recovery starts with what is still standing.
cards.reversedGeneral: Acceptance, moving on, seeing what remains, healing.
cards.imageDescription: A cloaked figure looks down at three spilled cups, two cups still standing behind, a river and a bridge to a distant keep.
cards.core: Three cups spilled, and grief looking only at those. But two still stand behind you, and the reading turns on remembering them.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Six of Cups
cards.uprightMeaning: Nostalgia, innocence, childhood memories, gifts, simple joy, reunion.
cards.reversedMeaning: Living in the past, inability to move forward, rose-tinted view.
cards.uprightLove: Simple joy, reunion, or a gift from an older innocence.
cards.uprightCareer: A reunion with an earlier, simpler way of working, or a gift from the past.
cards.uprightGeneral: Nostalgia, innocence, gifts, and simple joy.
cards.reversedLove: Living in the past keeps the bond from moving forward.
cards.reversedCareer: A rose-tinted view of old work blocks the next step.
cards.reversedGeneral: Living in the past, inability to move forward, or a rose-tinted view.
cards.imageDescription: A child offers a cup of white flowers to a smaller child in a walled garden, more flowered cups around, a guard walking away in the distance.
cards.core: Flowers passed between children in an old courtyard. Nostalgia, kindness, and the sweetness of what was innocent then.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Seven of Cups
cards.uprightMeaning: Choices, fantasy, illusion, many options, wishful thinking.
cards.reversedMeaning: Clarity emerging, decisive action, grounding of dreams, confusion clearing.
cards.uprightLove: Many glittering options in the heart. Some are fantasy.
cards.uprightCareer: Too many imagined paths at work. Wishful thinking is not a plan.
cards.uprightGeneral: Choices, fantasy, illusion, and many options.
cards.reversedLove: Clarity and a real choice in the bond. Dreams meet ground.
cards.reversedCareer: Decisive action. Confusion about the work is clearing.
cards.reversedGeneral: Clarity emerging, decisive action, grounding of dreams, confusion clearing.
cards.imageDescription: A silhouette faces seven cups in a cloud, each holding a different vision: a face, a veiled figure, a snake, a castle, jewels, a wreath, and a dragon.
cards.core: Seven cups floating in cloud, each promising something. Wishful thinking and too many choices, until one is pulled down to earth.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Eight of Cups
cards.uprightMeaning: Walking away, seeking deeper meaning, leaving what no longer serves.
cards.reversedMeaning: Fear of change, staying too long, avoidance, temporary return.
cards.uprightLove: Walking away from a bond that no longer serves, seeking deeper meaning.
cards.uprightCareer: Leave a role or project that is complete in form but empty in meaning.
cards.uprightGeneral: Walking away to seek deeper meaning. Leaving what no longer serves.
cards.reversedLove: Fear of change, or staying too long. A temporary return.
cards.reversedCareer: Avoidance of a needed exit at work, or a brief relapse into the old load.
cards.reversedGeneral: Fear of change, staying too long, avoidance, or a temporary return.
cards.imageDescription: A cloaked figure with a staff walks away from eight stacked cups toward rocky mountains under a moon that is both crescent and full.
cards.core: Cups stacked neatly and a figure walking uphill away from them. Leaving something emotionally invested because staying costs more.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Nine of Cups
cards.uprightMeaning: Contentment, wish fulfillment, emotional satisfaction, the wish card.
cards.reversedMeaning: Smugness, dissatisfaction despite abundance, unfulfilled desires.
cards.uprightLove: Emotional satisfaction and a wish met in the heart.
cards.uprightCareer: A wish fulfilled at work. Satisfaction with what has been built.
cards.uprightGeneral: Contentment, wish fulfillment, emotional satisfaction.
cards.reversedLove: Smugness, or a wish still empty despite plenty in the bond.
cards.reversedCareer: Dissatisfaction despite abundance at work. The desire is still unmet.
cards.reversedGeneral: Smugness, dissatisfaction despite abundance, or unfulfilled desires.
cards.imageDescription: A satisfied figure sits with arms crossed before a curved bench of nine covered cups, a red cap and a wooden platform.
cards.core: The full row behind a satisfied host: the wish card. Contentment earned, pleasure allowed, enough that is actually enough.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Ten of Cups
cards.uprightMeaning: Emotional fulfillment, family harmony, lasting happiness, dream of home.
cards.reversedMeaning: Disharmony at home, broken ideals, temporary happiness.
cards.uprightLove: Lasting happiness and a dream of home. Family harmony.
cards.uprightCareer: Fulfillment that reaches the whole house, well beyond the job.
cards.uprightGeneral: Emotional fulfillment, family harmony, lasting happiness.
cards.reversedLove: Disharmony at home or a broken ideal of the bond.
cards.reversedCareer: Happiness at work that does not last, or a house in conflict.
cards.reversedGeneral: Disharmony at home, broken ideals, or only temporary happiness.
cards.imageDescription: A couple stands with an arm around each other, two children dancing, a house and a river, a rainbow of ten cups in the sky.
cards.core: The arc of cups over a family under open sky. Emotional fulfillment shared, love as a settled home rather than a chase.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Page of Cups
cards.uprightMeaning: Emotional openness, intuitive messages, sensitivity, creative dreamer, gentle surprise.
cards.reversedMeaning: Emotional immaturity, insecurity, blocked intuition, disappointment.
cards.uprightLove: A gentle surprise or an intuitive message in the heart. Stay open.
cards.uprightCareer: A sensitive, creative first note at work. Listen for the odd message.
cards.uprightGeneral: Emotional openness, intuitive messages, a creative dreamer.
cards.reversedLove: Insecurity or immaturity in feeling. The message is blocked.
cards.reversedCareer: Disappointment or blocked intuition on a new brief.
cards.reversedGeneral: Emotional immaturity, insecurity, blocked intuition, or disappointment.
cards.imageDescription: A young figure in a tunic and beret holds a cup from which a fish emerges, standing at the edge of a sea.
cards.core: A student of water, fish rising from the cup. Small messages of feeling, creative surprises, the stance of an open heart learning.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Knight of Cups
cards.uprightMeaning: Romance, following the heart, idealist, charm, artistic pursuit.
cards.reversedMeaning: Moodiness, unrealistic expectations, emotional manipulation, disappointment.
cards.uprightLove: Romance and charm. An idealist following the heart.
cards.uprightCareer: An artistic pursuit led by feeling more than by a spreadsheet.
cards.uprightGeneral: Romance, following the heart, charm, artistic pursuit.
cards.reversedLove: Moodiness, unreal hopes, or emotional manipulation in the bond.
cards.reversedCareer: Disappointment when the ideal of the work meets the ground.
cards.reversedGeneral: Moodiness, unrealistic expectations, emotional manipulation, or disappointment.
cards.imageDescription: A knight in a winged helmet rides a horse at a walk, offering a cup, a river and rolling hills behind.
cards.core: Water in motion: the romantic on a slow horse, invitation in hand. Feeling made into an offer, ideals riding ahead of proof.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Queen of Cups
cards.uprightMeaning: Deep empathy, emotional intelligence, nurturing, calm presence, psychic sensitivity.
cards.reversedMeaning: Overwhelm by emotions, martyrdom, codependency, emotional instability.
cards.uprightLove: Deep empathy and a calm, nurturing presence in the bond.
cards.uprightCareer: Emotional intelligence as a way of leading. Feel, then decide.
cards.uprightGeneral: Deep empathy, emotional intelligence, a calm nurturing presence.
cards.reversedLove: Codependency, martyrdom, or overwhelm by feeling.
cards.reversedCareer: Emotional instability or martyrdom in the role.
cards.reversedGeneral: Overwhelm by emotions, martyrdom, codependency, or emotional instability.
cards.imageDescription: A crowned woman sits on a throne at the water's edge, gazing at an ornate closed cup, cherubs and mermaids on the throne, a calm sea.
cards.core: Water mastered inward: deep empathy, intuition, care that holds others without drowning. The heart that listens first.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: King of Cups
cards.uprightMeaning: Emotional maturity, balanced feeling and action, compassionate leadership, mastery of the inner world.
cards.reversedMeaning: Emotional coldness, moodiness, manipulation, repressed feelings.
cards.uprightLove: Mature, compassionate leadership of feeling in the bond.
cards.uprightCareer: Balance feeling and action. Lead the work without drowning in it.
cards.uprightGeneral: Emotional maturity, compassionate leadership, mastery of the inner world.
cards.reversedLove: Coldness, moodiness, or manipulation in the bond. Feeling is repressed.
cards.reversedCareer: A cold or moody hand on the work. Feeling used as a lever.
cards.reversedGeneral: Emotional coldness, moodiness, manipulation, or repressed feelings.
cards.imageDescription: A crowned man sits on a throne in a restless sea, a cup in one hand and a short scepter in the other, a ship and a leaping fish in the water.
cards.core: Water mastered outward: calm in the swell, feeling governed without being frozen. Compassion with a steady hand on the tiller.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Ace of Swords
uprightKeywords: new idea that cuts through confusion
cards.uprightMeaning: Mental clarity, breakthrough, truth, sharp insight, new idea that cuts through confusion.
cards.reversedMeaning: Confusion, chaos, misuse of intellect, brutality of words.
cards.uprightLove: A sharp truth that cuts through confusion in the bond.
cards.uprightCareer: A breakthrough idea. Clarity first, then the plan.
cards.uprightGeneral: Mental clarity, breakthrough, truth. A new idea that cuts through confusion.
cards.reversedLove: Brutal words or a misuse of intellect in the bond, leaving chaos where clarity should be.
cards.reversedCareer: Confusion or a sharp mind used as a weapon at work.
cards.reversedGeneral: Confusion, chaos, misuse of intellect, or brutality of words.
cards.imageDescription: A hand from a cloud holds an upright sword crowned with a wreath, six yods in the sky, a barren landscape and mountains below.
cards.core: A sword through the crown: sudden clarity, truth that cuts cleanly. A breakthrough of mind that asks to be used honestly.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Two of Swords
cards.uprightMeaning: Stalemate, difficult choice, avoidance, blind decision, need for balance.
cards.reversedMeaning: Decision forced, information revealed, moving past indecision.
cards.uprightLove: A stalemate or a choice avoided in the bond. Balance is needed.
cards.uprightCareer: A difficult choice at work, made while still half blind.
cards.uprightGeneral: Stalemate, a difficult choice, avoidance, a need for balance.
cards.reversedLove: Information comes in. The bond can move past indecision.
cards.reversedCareer: A decision is forced at work. The blindfold can come off.
cards.reversedGeneral: A decision forced, information revealed, moving past indecision.
cards.imageDescription: A seated blindfolded woman crosses two swords over her chest, a crescent moon and a rocky sea behind her.
cards.core: Blindfolded balance, two blades crossed over the chest. A stalemate held by refusing to look; the choice waits behind the blindfold.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Three of Swords
cards.uprightMeaning: Heartbreak, grief, painful truth, sorrow, separation.
cards.reversedMeaning: Recovery, forgiveness, releasing pain, healing after hurt.
cards.uprightLove: Heartbreak, sorrow, a painful truth, or a separation.
cards.uprightCareer: A painful truth about the work. Grief is honest here.
cards.uprightGeneral: Heartbreak, grief, painful truth, sorrow, separation.
cards.reversedLove: Forgiveness and healing after hurt in the bond.
cards.reversedCareer: Recovery after a hard truth at work. Release the pain.
cards.reversedGeneral: Recovery, forgiveness, releasing pain, healing after hurt.
cards.imageDescription: A red heart is pierced by three swords against a gray sky and falling rain. No figures.
cards.core: Three blades through a heart under rain: heartbreak, painful truth, sorrow named plainly. What is pierced can be tended once it is admitted.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Four of Swords
cards.uprightMeaning: Rest, recovery, contemplation, necessary pause after struggle.
cards.reversedMeaning: Restlessness, burnout, inability to rest, forced activity.
cards.uprightLove: A necessary pause after struggle. Rest the bond. Do not push.
cards.uprightCareer: Recovery time after a hard push. Contemplation before the next sprint.
cards.uprightGeneral: Rest, recovery, contemplation. A necessary pause after struggle.
cards.reversedLove: Restlessness or forced activity when the bond needed quiet.
cards.reversedCareer: Burnout from an inability to rest at work.
cards.reversedGeneral: Restlessness, burnout, inability to rest, or forced activity.
cards.imageDescription: A knight lies in repose on a tomb, hands in prayer, one sword beneath and three hung on the wall, a stained-glass window above.
cards.core: A figure at rest in a quiet chapel: retreat, recovery, deliberate stillness. Rest here is a strategy.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Five of Swords
cards.uprightMeaning: Conflict, hollow victory, win-at-all-costs, tension, defeat with cost.
cards.reversedMeaning: Desire to reconcile, release of conflict, learning from defeat.
cards.uprightLove: A hollow win in the bond. Tension, and a cost to the victory.
cards.uprightCareer: Win-at-all-costs at work. The victory may not be worth the field.
cards.uprightGeneral: Conflict, a hollow victory, tension, a defeat with cost.
cards.reversedLove: A desire to reconcile. Release the fight.
cards.reversedCareer: Learn from a costly win or loss. Put the swords down.
cards.reversedGeneral: A desire to reconcile, release of conflict, learning from defeat.
cards.imageDescription: A smirking figure gathers three swords, two more on the ground, two figures walk away toward a choppy sea and a gray sky.
cards.core: Swords collected while others walk away: a hollow victory. Winning the exchange and losing the room.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Six of Swords
cards.uprightMeaning: Transition, moving away from difficulty, gradual recovery, passage to calmer waters.
cards.reversedMeaning: Emotional baggage, resistance to transition, unfinished business.
cards.uprightLove: A passage toward calmer water in the bond. Recovery is gradual.
cards.uprightCareer: Moving the work away from difficulty. The crossing is underway.
cards.uprightGeneral: Transition, moving away from difficulty, a passage to calmer waters.
cards.reversedLove: Unfinished business or baggage keeps the bond in rough water.
cards.reversedCareer: Resistance to a needed transition at work.
cards.reversedGeneral: Emotional baggage, resistance to transition, or unfinished business.
cards.imageDescription: A ferryman poles a boat carrying a cloaked adult and a child, six swords standing in the hull, water rough on one side and calmer ahead.
cards.core: A ferry moving to calmer water, swords carried in the boat. Transition away from difficulty, the quiet, unglamorous crossing that heals.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Seven of Swords
cards.uprightMeaning: Strategy, deception, going it alone, theft of ideas, stealth.
cards.reversedMeaning: Coming clean, rethinking tactics, exposure of deception.
cards.uprightLove: Stealth or going it alone in the bond. Something is being carried off.
cards.uprightCareer: A solo strategy, or an idea taken without credit.
cards.uprightGeneral: Strategy, deception, going it alone, stealth.
cards.reversedLove: Coming clean. A deception in the bond is exposed or released.
cards.reversedCareer: Rethink the tactic. A stealth move at work comes into the light.
cards.reversedGeneral: Coming clean, rethinking tactics, or exposure of deception.
cards.imageDescription: A figure sneaks from a camp carrying five swords, two left standing, tents and figures in the distance, a look back over the shoulder.
cards.core: Five swords carried off on tiptoe: strategy, stealth, or getting away with something. The question is what the cleverness costs.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Eight of Swords
cards.uprightMeaning: Self-imposed restriction, mental prison, feeling trapped by beliefs, paralysis.
cards.reversedMeaning: New perspective, release, self-acceptance, finding freedom.
cards.uprightLove: A feeling of being trapped in the bond, often by a belief more than a lock.
cards.uprightCareer: Paralysis at work from a mental prison of your own making.
cards.uprightGeneral: Self-imposed restriction, a mental prison, paralysis.
cards.reversedLove: A new perspective frees the bond. The bind was mostly belief.
cards.reversedCareer: Release and self-acceptance. The work can move again.
cards.reversedGeneral: New perspective, release, self-acceptance, finding freedom.
cards.imageDescription: A blindfolded, bound woman stands in a puddle, eight swords planted around her like a cage, a castle on a barren rise behind. The binds are loose.
cards.core: Bound and blindfolded among planted blades, yet the feet are free. Restriction that is mostly believed rather than built.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Nine of Swords
cards.uprightMeaning: Anxiety, nightmares, worry, mental anguish, overthinking in the dark.
cards.reversedMeaning: Hope returning, seeking help, releasing worry, perspective gained.
cards.uprightLove: Anxiety and night-worry about the bond. The anguish is mental.
cards.uprightCareer: Overthinking the work in the dark. The fear is louder than the fact.
cards.uprightGeneral: Anxiety, nightmares, worry, mental anguish.
cards.reversedLove: Hope returning. Seek help and release the night-worry.
cards.reversedCareer: Perspective gained on a work fear. Help is allowed.
cards.reversedGeneral: Hope returning, seeking help, releasing worry, perspective gained.
cards.imageDescription: A figure sits up in bed covering the face, nine swords hang on the wall above, a quilt embroidered with roses and zodiac signs.
cards.core: Upright in bed at the worst hour, swords stacked on the dark. Anxiety's theater, grief at night, fears grown larger than their facts.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Ten of Swords
cards.uprightMeaning: Painful ending, rock bottom, betrayal or defeat, the worst is over.
cards.reversedMeaning: Recovery beginning, inevitable end accepted, only upward from here.
cards.uprightLove: A painful ending in the bond. Rock bottom, and the worst is over.
cards.uprightCareer: A defeat or betrayal at work. The chapter is done. The worst is over.
cards.uprightGeneral: A painful ending, rock bottom, betrayal or defeat. The worst is over.
cards.reversedLove: The end is accepted. Recovery in the heart can begin.
cards.reversedCareer: Only upward from here. Accept the close and start the next protocol.
cards.reversedGeneral: Recovery beginning, the inevitable end accepted, only upward from here.
cards.imageDescription: A figure lies face down with ten swords in the back, a black sky breaking to yellow dawn, a still sea and distant mountains.
cards.core: The lowest card in the deck, and behind it a sunrise. The ending is total, which means the worst is already over and the light is next.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Page of Swords
cards.uprightMeaning: Curiosity, mental energy, vigilance, new ideas, truth-seeking.
cards.reversedMeaning: Gossip, all talk no action, mental restlessness, manipulation of information.
cards.uprightLove: Curious, vigilant truth-seeking in the bond. Ask, do not assume.
cards.uprightCareer: New ideas and mental energy. Scout the brief. Stay sharp.
cards.uprightGeneral: Curiosity, mental energy, vigilance, truth-seeking.
cards.reversedLove: Gossip or restless talk without action in the bond.
cards.reversedCareer: Information twisted, or all talk and no move at work.
cards.reversedGeneral: Gossip, all talk no action, mental restlessness, or manipulation of information.
cards.imageDescription: A young figure stands on windswept ground holding a sword upright with both hands, clouds and birds in a restless sky, looking back over the shoulder.
cards.core: A student of air on watch: curiosity with a blade, questions, vigilance, news. The stance of a mind learning to cut fairly.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Knight of Swords
cards.uprightMeaning: Fast action, direct communication, defending beliefs, intellectual drive.
cards.reversedMeaning: Reckless words, disregard for consequences, aggression, lack of direction.
cards.uprightLove: Direct, fast words in the bond. Beliefs are being defended.
cards.uprightCareer: Intellectual drive and fast action. Say the true thing, then move.
cards.uprightGeneral: Fast action, direct communication, defending beliefs.
cards.reversedLove: Reckless words or aggression in the bond, without a line.
cards.reversedCareer: A charge at work with no aim, and no care for the consequence.
cards.reversedGeneral: Reckless words, disregard for consequences, aggression, or a lack of direction.
cards.imageDescription: An armored knight charges on a galloping horse, sword raised, a torn sky and windswept trees, the horse's mane flying.
cards.core: Air at full charge: brilliant, blunt, and fast. Argument as cavalry, truth delivered at a speed that can wound.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Queen of Swords
cards.uprightMeaning: Clear-minded, perceptive, independent, honest communication, boundaries.
cards.reversedMeaning: Coldness, bitterness, overly critical, emotional detachment used as weapon.
cards.uprightLove: Honest, independent, clear-minded speech and firm boundaries in the bond.
cards.uprightCareer: Perceptive, honest communication. Cut the fog. Keep the boundary.
cards.uprightGeneral: Clear-minded, perceptive, independent, honest, boundaried.
cards.reversedLove: Coldness or a critical edge used as a weapon in the bond.
cards.reversedCareer: Bitterness or detachment used to control the work conversation.
cards.reversedGeneral: Coldness, bitterness, an overly critical stance, or detachment used as a weapon.
cards.imageDescription: A crowned woman sits in profile on a carved throne, a sword upright in her right hand, her left extended, a single bird in a clear sky, clouds at her feet.
cards.core: Air mastered inward: clear-eyed honesty sharpened by experience. Boundaries drawn cleanly, sentiment never mistaken for truth.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: King of Swords
cards.uprightMeaning: Intellectual authority, truth, discipline, fair judgment, clear thinking.
cards.reversedMeaning: Manipulation, cruelty, misuse of power, cold rationality without heart.
cards.uprightLove: Fair judgment and clear thinking in the bond. Truth with discipline.
cards.uprightCareer: Intellectual authority and fair judgment. Think clearly, then rule.
cards.uprightGeneral: Intellectual authority, truth, discipline, fair judgment.
cards.reversedLove: Cruelty or cold rationality without heart in the bond.
cards.reversedCareer: A misuse of mental power at work. Manipulation dressed as reason.
cards.reversedGeneral: Manipulation, cruelty, misuse of power, or cold rationality without heart.
cards.imageDescription: A crowned man sits on a throne carved with butterflies and moons, an upright sword in his right hand, a stern gaze, trees and clouds behind.
cards.core: Air mastered outward: judgment, standards, the rule of reason. Authority that lives or dies by its own fairness.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Ace of Pentacles
cards.uprightMeaning: New material opportunity, prosperity seed, practical beginning, grounded potential.
cards.reversedMeaning: Missed opportunity, poor planning, lack of follow-through, financial delay.
cards.uprightLove: A practical new beginning that can support a life together.
cards.uprightCareer: A seed of prosperity. A grounded, material opening. Follow through.
cards.uprightGeneral: A new material opportunity and a practical beginning. Grounded potential.
cards.reversedLove: A missed material opening in the bond, or no follow-through.
cards.reversedCareer: Poor planning or a financial delay. The seed was not planted.
cards.reversedGeneral: Missed opportunity, poor planning, lack of follow-through, or financial delay.
cards.imageDescription: A hand from a cloud holds a large pentacle over a garden path through an arched hedge, mountains in the distance, lilies in the grass.
cards.core: A coin offered from a cloud over a kept garden: a tangible new opportunity. Seed money, a first foothold, matter ready to grow.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Two of Pentacles
cards.uprightMeaning: Balancing priorities, adaptability, juggling resources, flexibility.
cards.reversedMeaning: Overwhelm, disorganization, loss of balance, difficulty managing change.
cards.uprightLove: Juggling two claims on the heart. Flexibility is the skill.
cards.uprightCareer: Balance priorities and resources. Adapt as the ships pitch.
cards.uprightGeneral: Balancing priorities, adaptability, juggling resources.
cards.reversedLove: Overwhelm or a loss of balance in the bond.
cards.reversedCareer: Disorganization and trouble managing change at work.
cards.reversedGeneral: Overwhelm, disorganization, loss of balance, or difficulty managing change.
cards.imageDescription: A dancing figure juggles two pentacles inside an infinity loop, two ships on a high sea behind, a tall hat and a casual stance.
cards.core: Two coins juggled inside a figure eight while ships ride the swell. Balance in motion, priorities traded moment to moment.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Three of Pentacles
cards.uprightMeaning: Teamwork, collaboration, skill-building, recognition of craft, shared goals.
cards.reversedMeaning: Lack of teamwork, poor collaboration, mediocrity, group conflict.
cards.uprightLove: Building something together. Craft and shared goals.
cards.uprightCareer: Teamwork and recognition of skill. The work is a collaboration.
cards.uprightGeneral: Teamwork, collaboration, skill-building, recognition of craft.
cards.reversedLove: Poor collaboration or conflict about how the life is built.
cards.reversedCareer: Mediocrity or a team that will not work as one.
cards.reversedGeneral: Lack of teamwork, poor collaboration, mediocrity, or group conflict.
cards.imageDescription: A mason on a bench works on a cathedral arch, a monk and a noble consult a plan, three pentacles set in the architecture.
cards.core: The craftsman, the architect, and the patron at one arch. Skilled work recognized, collaboration that builds something that lasts.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Four of Pentacles
reversedKeywords: inability to share or spend wisely
cards.uprightMeaning: Security, conservation, holding on, financial stability, control of resources.
cards.reversedMeaning: Greed, possessiveness, fear of loss, inability to share or spend wisely.
cards.uprightLove: Holding on for security. Control of what is shared.
cards.uprightCareer: Financial stability through conservation. Watch the grip.
cards.uprightGeneral: Security, conservation, holding on, control of resources.
cards.reversedLove: Possessiveness or a fear of loss in the bond. The grip is too tight.
cards.reversedCareer: Greed, or an inability to share or spend wisely at work.
cards.reversedGeneral: Greed, possessiveness, fear of loss, or an inability to share or spend wisely.
cards.imageDescription: A seated figure holds a pentacle against the chest, one under each foot and one on the crown, a city behind, a closed, guarded posture.
cards.core: Coins gripped at crown, heart, and feet. Security held so tightly it stops circulating; stability shading into hoarding.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Five of Pentacles
cards.uprightMeaning: Hardship, insecurity, feeling left out, material or health struggle.
cards.reversedMeaning: Recovery, help arriving, improvement, end of isolation.
cards.uprightLove: A feeling of being left out, or a material strain on the bond.
cards.uprightCareer: Hardship or insecurity at work. Help may be closer than it looks.
cards.uprightGeneral: Hardship, insecurity, feeling left out, a material or health struggle.
cards.reversedLove: Help arriving. Isolation in the bond can end.
cards.reversedCareer: Recovery and improvement. The lean season is turning.
cards.reversedGeneral: Recovery, help arriving, improvement, an end of isolation.
cards.imageDescription: Two figures in rags pass through snow outside a lit church window of five pentacles, one on crutches, neither looking up at the light.
cards.core: Two figures in the snow outside a lit window. Hardship and feeling shut out, with help nearer than it looks, if it is asked for.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Six of Pentacles
cards.uprightMeaning: Generosity, charity, balanced giving and receiving, support.
cards.reversedMeaning: Strings attached, imbalance of power, stinginess or over-giving.
cards.uprightLove: Balanced giving and receiving. Support without a hidden price.
cards.uprightCareer: Generosity and fair support. Watch the scale.
cards.uprightGeneral: Generosity, charity, balanced giving and receiving.
cards.reversedLove: Strings attached, or an imbalance of power in the bond.
cards.reversedCareer: Stinginess or over-giving at work. The scale is off.
cards.reversedGeneral: Strings attached, imbalance of power, stinginess, or over-giving.
cards.imageDescription: A standing merchant holds a scale and drops coins into the hands of one of two kneeling figures, six pentacles in the air, a town behind.
cards.core: Coins weighed and given by hand. Generosity, fairness, and the balance of giving and receiving, including toward yourself.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Seven of Pentacles
cards.uprightMeaning: Assessment, patience, long-term investment, evaluating progress.
cards.reversedMeaning: Impatience, lack of results, wasted effort, need to change approach.
cards.uprightLove: A pause to evaluate whether the bond is growing as planted.
cards.uprightCareer: Long-term investment. Assess the crop before the next push.
cards.uprightGeneral: Assessment, patience, long-term investment, evaluating progress.
cards.reversedLove: Impatience with the pace of the bond, or a sense of wasted care.
cards.reversedCareer: Lack of results. Change the approach rather than only waiting.
cards.reversedGeneral: Impatience, lack of results, wasted effort, or a need to change approach.
cards.imageDescription: A farmer leans on a hoe and studies a bush bearing six pentacles, a seventh at the roots, a look of tired appraisal.
cards.core: Leaning on the hoe, counting the vine's coins. Patience at the midpoint: assess the investment, then tend or replant.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Eight of Pentacles
cards.uprightMeaning: Craftsmanship, diligence, skill development, focused work, mastery through practice.
cards.reversedMeaning: Lack of motivation, poor quality, boredom, uninspired effort.
cards.uprightLove: Diligent practice in how you show up. Craft over grand gestures.
cards.uprightCareer: Focused skill-building. Mastery through repetition.
cards.uprightGeneral: Craftsmanship, diligence, focused work, mastery through practice.
cards.reversedLove: Boredom or uninspired effort in the bond. The craft has gone slack.
cards.reversedCareer: Poor quality or no motivation on the workbench.
cards.reversedGeneral: Lack of motivation, poor quality, boredom, or uninspired effort.
cards.imageDescription: A craftsman sits at a bench hammering a pentacle, six finished coins hang on a post, an eighth on the ground, a town in the distance.
cards.core: Coin after coin carved at the bench: craft, diligence, mastery built one repetition at a time.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Nine of Pentacles
cards.uprightMeaning: Self-sufficiency, luxury earned, independence, enjoyment of results, refinement.
cards.reversedMeaning: Over-spending, dependence, superficial success, isolation in wealth.
cards.uprightLove: Independence and a refined enjoyment of what you have grown.
cards.uprightCareer: Earned luxury and self-sufficiency. Enjoy the result of the work.
cards.uprightGeneral: Self-sufficiency, earned luxury, independence, enjoyment of results.
cards.reversedLove: Dependence, or isolation inside plenty, cools the bond.
cards.reversedCareer: Over-spending or a success that is only surface.
cards.reversedGeneral: Over-spending, dependence, superficial success, or isolation in wealth.
cards.imageDescription: A woman in a rich gown stands in a vineyard of nine pentacles, a hooded bird on her glove, a snail at her feet, a manor behind.
cards.core: A garden earned, a falcon gloved: self-sufficiency and refined comfort. Independence that was paid for honestly.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Ten of Pentacles
cards.uprightMeaning: Legacy, long-term security, family wealth or tradition, culmination of material efforts.
cards.reversedMeaning: Instability, family financial conflict, fleeting success, lack of lasting foundation.
cards.uprightLove: Long-term security and a family or household legacy in the bond.
cards.uprightCareer: Culmination of material effort. A foundation built to last.
cards.uprightGeneral: Legacy, long-term security, family tradition, a material culmination.
cards.reversedLove: Family conflict over resources, or no lasting foundation for the bond.
cards.reversedCareer: Instability or fleeting success at work. The base is thin.
cards.reversedGeneral: Instability, family financial conflict, fleeting success, or no lasting foundation.
cards.imageDescription: An old man in a patterned robe sits with dogs at a city gate, a couple and a child beyond, a family crest, ten pentacles arranged over the scene.
cards.core: Three generations, dogs, arch, and coins: legacy. Wealth as continuity, what outlasts the person who built it.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Page of Pentacles
cards.uprightMeaning: Student energy, new practical opportunity, diligence, ambition to learn and build.
cards.reversedMeaning: Lack of commitment, procrastination, poor focus on material goals.
cards.uprightLove: A diligent, student willingness to learn how to build a life together.
cards.uprightCareer: A new practical opportunity. Study it. Then build.
cards.uprightGeneral: Student energy, a practical opening, diligence, ambition to learn and build.
cards.reversedLove: Procrastination or a lack of commitment in the bond.
cards.reversedCareer: Poor focus on the material goal. The study has stalled.
cards.reversedGeneral: Lack of commitment, procrastination, or poor focus on material goals.
