cards.imageDescription: A young figure stands in a green field studying a pentacle held up in both hands, trees and a distant plowland, a yellow sky.
cards.core: A student of earth holding the coin up to the light. Study, apprenticeship, small beginnings taken seriously.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Knight of Pentacles
cards.uprightMeaning: Reliable, hardworking, methodical, responsible, steady progress.
cards.reversedMeaning: Stubbornness, laziness, overly slow, perfectionism that blocks progress.
cards.uprightLove: Reliable, methodical care, steady week after week.
cards.uprightCareer: Hardworking, responsible progress. One field at a time.
cards.uprightGeneral: Reliable, hardworking, methodical, responsible, steady progress.
cards.reversedLove: Stubborn slowness or a perfectionism that stalls the bond.
cards.reversedCareer: Laziness, or so slow and perfect that the work never ships.
cards.reversedGeneral: Stubbornness, laziness, overly slow pace, or perfectionism that blocks progress.
cards.imageDescription: A knight sits a heavy horse at rest, a pentacle held up in one hand, a freshly plowed field around, a still, watchful posture.
cards.core: Earth at a walk: the slowest knight and the one who arrives. Method, patience, and work that does not need applause.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: Queen of Pentacles
cards.uprightMeaning: Practical nurturing, financial security, comfort, resourcefulness, down-to-earth care.
cards.reversedMeaning: Self-neglect, smothering practicality, materialism, insecurity about resources.
cards.uprightLove: Down-to-earth care and practical comfort in the bond.
cards.uprightCareer: Resourceful, secure, practical leadership of the material side.
cards.uprightGeneral: Practical nurturing, financial security, comfort, resourcefulness.
cards.reversedLove: Self-neglect or smothering practicality. Insecurity about what you have.
cards.reversedCareer: Materialism or self-neglect while tending everyone else's resources.
cards.reversedGeneral: Self-neglect, smothering practicality, materialism, or insecurity about resources.
cards.imageDescription: A crowned woman sits in a lush garden holding a pentacle in her lap, a rabbit at her feet, fruit, flowers, and a distant mountain.
cards.core: Earth mastered inward: practical nurture, a warm hearth run by capable hands. Care expressed as competence.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: King of Pentacles
cards.uprightMeaning: Abundance, successful provider, business mastery, security, grounded leadership.
cards.reversedMeaning: Greed, materialism, stubbornness, status obsession, poor financial judgment.
cards.uprightLove: A successful, grounded provider energy. Security in the bond.
cards.uprightCareer: Business mastery and grounded leadership. Abundance with a base.
cards.uprightGeneral: Abundance, successful provision, security, grounded leadership.
cards.reversedLove: Greed, status, or stubborn materialism warps the bond.
cards.reversedCareer: Poor financial judgment or a status obsession at work.
cards.reversedGeneral: Greed, materialism, stubbornness, status obsession, or poor financial judgment.
cards.imageDescription: A crowned man in a rich robe sits on a carved throne holding a pentacle and a scepter, grapes and bulls on the throne, a castle and garden behind.
cards.core: Earth mastered outward: the proven builder in a grown garden. Prosperity governed steadily, wealth as stewardship.
cards.credit: Illustrations by Pamela Colman Smith, 1909 (public domain).

cards.name: The Instrument
cards.uprightMeaning: This position is about the method, the observer, or contamination. The lens is in the frame. It is a note about the experiment itself.
cards.reversedMeaning: The Instrument does not reverse. The lens stays in the frame. This remains a note about the method, the observer, or contamination.
cards.core: The lens is in the frame.
cards.uprightLove: A note about how you are looking at the bond. It says nothing about the other person.
cards.uprightCareer: A calibration of the protocol. Check the method before you read the result as a career omen.
cards.uprightGeneral: This position is about the method, the observer, or contamination. It predicts nothing.
cards.reversedLove: The Instrument does not reverse. It stays a note about how you are looking at the bond.
cards.reversedCareer: The Instrument does not reverse. It stays a note about the experiment itself.
cards.reversedGeneral: The Instrument does not reverse. The lens stays in the frame.
cards.imageDescription: Original GhostLab art: a mint lens and reticle centered on a navy field. No cliff, traveler, or fool imagery.
cards.credit: GhostLab Field Deck, Adirondack Cyber Security.
